entities.summary: Louis Roy Groza, nicknamed "the Toe", was an American professional football offensive tackle and placekicker while playing his entire career for the Cleveland Browns in the All-America Football Conference (AAFC) and National Football League (NFL). Groza was professional football's career kicking and points leader when he retired after the 1967 season. He played in 21 seasons for the Browns, helping the team to win eight league championships in that span. Groza's accuracy and strength as a kicker influenced the development of place-kicking as a specialty; he could kick field goals from beyond 50 yards (46 m) at a time when attempts from that distance were a rarity.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a kicker and placekicker for the Cleveland Browns, Lou Groza set numerous records that influenced the development of kicking in football, including holding the career record for most points scored until his retirement. His impact on the sport helped shape its modern strategy.
